planting.note: Root two-node stem cuttings in damp sphagnum or perlite mix under high humidity; established plants root slowly compared to other hoyas.

directions: A miniature Bornean hoya with small, thick, rounded leaves splashed irregularly in cream and mint-white over a deep green base, giving the trailing stems a frosted, mottled look that inspired the cultivar name. Grow in bright, filtered light in a chunky, fast-draining mix, letting the substrate dry between waterings since the fleshy leaves store moisture like a succulent. Mature vines produce small, tight clusters of star-shaped, pale flowers with a faint sweet scent, though this cultivar is grown primarily for its foliage. It is slower and more compact than the straight species, making it well suited to a small pot or shallow dish before it is given room to trail.

planting.note: Propagate from stem cuttings with at least one node; new growth emerges reddish-bronze before hardening to green.

directions: A Bornean climbing species valued for its broad, softly felted leaves covered in fine hairs that catch the light, with new growth emerging in coppery-red tones before maturing to a dusty green. Grow in bright, indirect light in a coarse, well-aerated mix on a support such as a pole or trellis, since it climbs more vigorously than many trailing hoya species. Clusters of small, pale yellow-green, star-shaped flowers with a musky scent appear on older growth once the vine is well established; avoid removing the woody spurs, as they rebloom for years. Allow the mix to dry between waterings and keep humidity moderate to high to prevent leaf-edge browning.

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in a well-drained mix; long, unbranched stems are easiest to propagate in multi-node sections.

directions: A slender, trailing hoya with long, narrow, grass-like leaves borne densely along thin, wiry stems, giving hanging specimens a fine-textured, curtain-like effect distinct from the broader-leaved carnosa types. Grow in bright, filtered light in a fast-draining succulent-style mix and allow it to dry out between waterings, as the narrow leaves have limited water storage compared to fleshier species. Small, star-shaped, white to pale pink flowers with a light fragrance form in loose clusters along the mature stem length. It is best displayed in a hanging basket where the long trailing stems can cascade freely without a support.

planting.note: Root two-node stem cuttings in perlite or a coarse bark mix under warm, humid conditions.

directions: A Philippine species with glossy, elliptic leaves and a modest, well-behaved climbing habit, making it a manageable choice for growers who want species diversity without a rampant vine. Grow in bright, indirect light in a chunky, fast-draining mix and let the substrate dry between waterings, since the leaves are only lightly succulent. Umbels of small, waxy, star-shaped flowers in soft pink to cream tones appear on spur growth once the plant reaches maturity, carrying a mild sweet fragrance. Provide a small trellis or moss pole to support the twining stems as the plant fills out.

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in a well-drained bark or perlite mix; vigorous vines benefit from a support to climb early.

directions: Native to the Banda Islands of Indonesia, this vigorous climber has thick, glossy, dark green leaves and can grow considerably larger than compact houseplant hoyas when given a tall support. Grow in bright, indirect light in a coarse, fast-draining mix and let it dry somewhat between waterings, increasing humidity slightly during active growth. Large, rounded umbels of waxy, star-shaped flowers in pale cream to yellow-green appear on mature spurs and carry a sweet evening fragrance typical of the genus. Because of its climbing vigor, it is best grown on a trellis or moss pole rather than left to trail from a hanging basket.

planting.note: Root single-node cuttings in damp sphagnum under high humidity; this species is slower to establish than most trade hoyas.

directions: A slow-growing collector species with large, thick, softly felted leaves marked by prominent, sunken silvery veins that stand out sharply against the deep green leaf surface, a texture reminiscent of Hoya sigillatis but with a broader, more rounded leaf shape. Grow in bright, filtered light with high humidity in a very open, chunky mix, since the fleshy leaves are prone to rot if the substrate stays wet. It flowers less readily in cultivation than more common species, but mature plants can produce small clusters of fuzzy, star-shaped flowers on woody spurs. Because of its slow habit, it is best grown in a small pot on a short support rather than a large hanging basket.

planting.note: Root two-node stem cuttings in a well-drained mix; variegated sections should be retained on each cutting to keep the pattern true.

directions: A variegated cultivar of the large-leaved macrophylla species, with broad, oval leaves edged and streaked in creamy white to pale yellow around a soft green center, giving each leaf a hand-painted look. Grow in bright, indirect light in a chunky, fast-draining mix, since the variegated tissue is more prone to sunburn in direct sun and to fading in low light. Established vines can produce clusters of soft pink, star-shaped, fragrant flowers, though the plant is grown chiefly for its bold, oversized foliage. Provide a support for the twining stems and let the mix dry between waterings, as with other semi-succulent hoyas.

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in a coarse, well-drained mix; keep warm and humid until new growth confirms establishment.

directions: A Southeast Asian species with thick, succulent, oblong leaves whose edges ripple and undulate distinctly, giving each leaf a crinkled, wavy outline unlike the flat leaves of most common trade hoyas. Grow in bright, filtered light in a very open, fast-draining mix and let it dry between waterings, since the fleshy leaves store water readily and are prone to rot in soggy conditions. Clusters of small, waxy, star-shaped flowers form on mature spur growth, typically in pale pink to cream shades with a mild fragrance. It has a modest climbing to trailing habit and does well with a small support or in a hanging pot once established.
